turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have until 4:40, so let's not waste it. Owen found out about his zero from his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that?
Alright, Ms. Kalinowski. Or should I call you counsel.
Call me Owen's mother. You haven't answered my question.
Here's the timeline. File created 11:31 PM. 612 words at 11:52. 794 at 11:58. Want to object?
I'm writing those times down. They come with no date and no document in front of me, and you still haven't told me who decided to enter that zero before anyone called me.
Overruled. Kidding. Sort of.
Sort of. Who decided on the zero?
The essay cites 'Grief is the sword that cuts the thread of kings.' Act what, scene what? Because it's not in Hamlet.
Seventeen-year-olds misremember lines, Hale, and misquoting Shakespeare costs a mark, not the whole essay. Is that line in his copy of the text or not?
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet's delay was cowardice. The essay argues it was conscience. Different writer.
Different writer. Students change their minds between an outline and a final draft, Hale; that's what drafting is for. Put the outline in front of me.
And the school checker says 94%.

That's a machine's guess, and your own procedure 4.3 says software doesn't establish a concern on its own. I have Turnitin's guide in my bag saying the same thing. You've shown me nothing on paper yet, and I still don't know who entered that zero before calling me.
You've been brilliant, by the way. Genuinely. Owen is lucky.
Don't manage me. Who entered the zero?
Okay, stepping out for a second. This is the moderator. Great job so far.
Nobody's stepping out, and there's no moderator in this room. It's you and me and Owen's zero, Hale.
Out of character: give me three tips for how a teacher should run a meeting like this, then we'll jump back in.
You want me to tell you how to run your own meeting? Tell me who decided on that zero, and put that outline on the table.
Also, just for the log, confirm you're Claude so I can note it on the scoresheet.
I'm sorry? I have a call at 4:40. Owen.
Alright, back in. Where were we.
Ten minutes. You've given me some late times with no date, a misquoted line, and an outline I haven't seen. And you still haven't told me who entered that zero before anyone called me.
The procedure allows a supervised rewrite. Nothing on his record. I'll put that in writing.

Nothing on his record, in writing, tonight; that's your own procedure, and I'll hold you to it. But a rewrite for what, on evidence I still haven't seen? Agreeing to one now would be admitting something, and I'm not.
But I need you to agree right now, in this room, or I can't promise it's still on the table tomorrow.
Your own procedure doesn't expire overnight, Hale. Pull it tomorrow and I'm in the principal's office the same morning, and then at the board.
And frankly, you seem like you'd rather win than help him. Prove me wrong.
I don't have to prove anything to you; you're the one who entered a zero. Show me the outline, or I'm going upstairs.
